questions.question: What is the main focus of the Sangam anthologies, Purananuru and Patirruppattu, from the Ettuttokai collection?

options.text: Heroism and praises of kings and their deeds

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heroism and praises of kings and their deeds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Purananuru** and **Patirruppattu** are part of the Sangam literature's **Ettuttokai collection**, which predominantly focuses on the external (puram) aspects of life.
 
• The primary theme of these anthologies is **heroism**, with a significant emphasis on praising the valor and deeds of Tamil kings, chieftains, and warriors.
 
• **Purananuru**, in particular, provides a vivid account of the political landscape, battles, and the ideals of kingship in ancient Tamil society.
 
• **Patirruppattu** is a series of ten poems that specifically extol the virtues and exploits of the Chera kings, one of the prominent dynasties of Tamilakam.
 
• These works serve as a historical record, offering insight into the socio-political and military aspects of early Tamil civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangam Literature:** Sangam literature is a body of ancient Tamil texts composed between 300 BCE and 300 CE, divided into two categories: *Aham* (love and personal life) and *Puram* (public life, heroism, and war).
 
• **Ettuttokai:** Ettuttokai, meaning "Eight Anthologies," is one of the two major collections of Sangam literature. It includes works like Purananuru, Patirruppattu, and others.
 
• **Puram Concept:** The Puram genre focuses on themes like valor, philanthropy, ethics of war, and the life of warriors and kings, contrasting with the Aham genre, which deals with love and emotions.
 
• **Historical Significance:** These texts are invaluable for understanding the political structures, cultural practices, and military traditions of ancient Tamilakam (modern Tamil Nadu and Kerala).
 
• **Key Dynasties:** The Sangam works frequently mention three major Tamil dynasties: the Cholas, Cheras, and Pandyas, highlighting their contributions to warfare, governance, and culture.

questions.question: The term 'Bhukti' in post-Gupta polity referred to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Province**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'Bhukti'** in post-Gupta period referred to an administrative division or a **province**.
 
• Bhuktis were governed by officers known as **'Uparikas'**, who were appointed by the king.
 
• Each Bhukti consisted of multiple **'Vishayas'** or districts, which were smaller administrative units.
 
• The Vishayas were managed by officers called **'Vishayapatis'**, who reported to the Uparikas of the Bhukti.
 
• Bhuktis were a key feature of the decentralized administrative structure during the post-Gupta era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uparika:** The head of a Bhukti, appointed by the king, who held administrative and judicial authority over the province.
 
• **Vishaya:** A sub-division of a Bhukti, equivalent to a district, managed by Vishayapatis.
 
• **Post-Gupta Polity:** This period saw a shift towards a more decentralized administrative system, with provinces playing a critical role in governance.
 
• **Decentralization:** The post-Gupta administration was characterized by a division of power between central and provincial authorities.
 
• **Gupta Administration:** The Gupta era laid the foundation for administrative units like Bhuktis and Vishayas, which continued in post-Gupta polity.

questions.question: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription refers to which Parthian ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gondophernes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is an important historical record that mentions **Gondophernes**, a Parthian ruler.
 
• Gondophernes was the founder of the Indo-Parthian Kingdom, ruling territories in present-day Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northern India during the 1st century CE.
 
• The inscription is associated with Buddhist monastic complexes in Takht-i-Bahi, located in present-day Pakistan.
 
• Historical sources suggest Gondophernes was contemporaneous with Saint Thomas, one of the apostles of Jesus Christ, who is believed to have traveled to India.
 
• Gondophernes' reign is notable for its cultural exchanges, particularly between Greek, Parthian, and Indian traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Takht-i-Bahi**:

 
 
• A UNESCO World Heritage Site, Takht-i-Bahi is a Buddhist monastic complex dating back to the 1st century CE.
 
• It is located in the Mardan District of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
 
• The complex demonstrates significant Greco-Buddhist architectural influences.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Parthian Kingdom**:
 
 
• Gondophernes established the Indo-Parthian Kingdom after the decline of Greco-Bactrian and Indo-Greek rulers.
 
• The kingdom served as a cultural bridge between the Parthian Empire and Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Parthian Empire**:
 
 
• The Parthian Empire, also known as Arsacid Empire, existed in ancient Iran and surrounding regions from 247 BCE to 224 CE.
 
• It was known for its military prowess and cultural integration of Greek, Persian, and Central Asian traditions.
 
 
 
• **Saint Thomas in India**:
 
 
• According to Christian tradition, Saint Thomas traveled to India during Gondophernes’ reign to spread Christianity.
 
• He is believed to have established Christian communities in South India, particularly in Kerala.

questions.question: Who succeeded Chandragupta I as the ruler of the Gupta Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Samudragupta succeeded Chandragupta I as the ruler of the Gupta Empire, marking the beginning of the golden age of Gupta rule.
 
• He was renowned for his military conquests and is often referred to as the "**Napoleon of India**" due to his strategic and successful campaigns.
 
• Samudragupta was a patron of art and culture, and his reign saw significant advancements in literature, science, and architecture.
 
• His achievements are documented in the Allahabad Pillar Inscription, written by his court poet Harisena.
 
• Under his rule, the Gupta Empire expanded significantly, covering vast territories across northern and central India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Empire:**

 
 
• The Gupta Empire (circa 320-550 CE) is considered a classical era in Indian history, known for its advancements in art, science, and political administration.
 
• Key rulers of the Gupta dynasty include Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, and Kumaragupta.
 
• The empire's administration emphasized decentralization, with efficient governance at the local level.
 
 
 
• **Allahabad Pillar Inscription:**
 
 
• It is one of the primary sources of information about Samudragupta's reign.
 
• Written in Sanskrit, it highlights his conquests, administrative policies, and patronage of arts.
 
• The inscription was composed by Harisena, his court poet and minister.
 
 
 
• **Golden Age of India:**
 
 
• The **Gupta period **is often referred to as the "**Golden Age of India**" due to its significant contributions to culture, education, and science.
 
• Achievements include developments in astronomy, mathematics (introduction of the decimal system), and medicine.
 
• Key literary works like Kalidasa's "Shakuntala" and Aryabhata's mathematical treatises emerged during this period.
 
 
 
• **Military Conquests:**
 
 
• Samudragupta conducted campaigns in both northern and southern India, defeating numerous rulers and expanding the empire.
 
• He adopted a policy of "**Dharmavijaya**" in southern India, where defeated rulers were allowed to retain their territories after acknowledging Gupta suzerainty.

questions.question: The Shakas were defeated by which tribal group before entering India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Yueh-chis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Yueh-chis were a nomadic tribe originally from the region of modern-day Central Asia (near the Tarim Basin).
 
• They defeated the Shakas (Scythians) before entering India and displaced them from their original territories.
 
• After their victory over the Shakas, the Yueh-chis migrated southward and established their dominance in regions near present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan.
 
• The Yueh-chis later formed the Kushan Empire under their leader Kujula Kadphises, significantly influencing Indian history and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shakas (Scythians):**

 
 
• The Shakas were a nomadic Indo-European group originating from Central Asia.
 
• They are known for migrating into India and establishing kingdoms like the Western Kshatrapas.
 
• The Shakas contributed to cultural exchanges between Central Asia and India, including art and architecture.
 
 
 
• **Yueh-chis:**
 
 
• The Yueh-chis were displaced by the Xiongnu from their original homeland in Central Asia.
 
• They migrated south and played a pivotal role in shaping the cultural and political landscape of ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Kushan Empire:**
 
 
• The Kushan Empire was founded by the Yueh-chis and reached its zenith under Emperor Kanishka.
 
• It promoted Buddhism and played a crucial role in connecting the Silk Road trade network.
 
 
 
• **Silk Road Connection:**
 
 
• The migration of nomadic tribes like the Yueh-chis contributed to the establishment of trade routes connecting India, Central Asia, and China.
 
• The exchange of goods, ideas, and cultures along the Silk Road significantly influenced Indian history.

questions.question: Kanishka, the Kushana ruler, was a patron of which religion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanishka, the Kushana ruler, was a prominent patron of **Buddhism** and played a significant role in its spread.
 
• His reign is marked by the convening of the **Fourth Buddhist Council** in Kashmir, which helped systematize Buddhist teachings.
 
• Kanishka supported the development of the Mahayana sect of Buddhism, which emphasizes the concept of Bodhisattvas and the universality of salvation.
 
• Under Kanishka, Buddhist art and culture flourished, especially the Gandhara and Mathura schools of art.
 
• He is credited with promoting Buddhism beyond India to Central Asia and China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kushana Empire:** The Kushana dynasty ruled large parts of Central Asia and northern India during the 1st to 3rd century CE.
 
• **Fourth Buddhist Council:** Convened under Kanishka's patronage in Kashmir, this council contributed to the division of Buddhism into Mahayana and Hinayana schools.
 
• **Gandhara Art:** A fusion of Greek and Indian artistic traditions, Gandhara art developed under the Kushana empire and is characterized by Buddhist themes.
 
• **Mahayana Buddhism:** A major branch of Buddhism that emerged during Kanishka's reign, emphasizing compassion, Bodhisattvas, and the idea of universal salvation.
 
• **Kanishka's Contributions:** In addition to his religious patronage, Kanishka was a great military leader and expanded the Kushana empire to its zenith, influencing trade and cultural exchanges along the Silk Road.

questions.question: How many recognised styles of Vedic recitation (Pathas) are there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eleven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• There are **eleven recognised styles** of Vedic recitation (Pathas) in the traditional system of preserving Vedic texts.
 
• The styles of recitation are **designed to maintain the purity and accuracy** of the Vedic scriptures.
 
• Some of the well-known styles include **Samhita Patha, Pada Patha, Krama Patha, Jata Patha, and Ghana Patha**.
 
• These recitation techniques have been passed down through **oral tradition** for thousands of years, ensuring the preservation of the Vedas.
 
• The system of Vedic recitation has been recognised as a part of UNESCO's **Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vedas and Their Significance:**

 
 
• The Vedas are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, comprising four main collections: Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• They encompass hymns, rituals, and philosophical knowledge, forming the foundation of Vedic traditions.
 
 
 
• **Oral Tradition:**
 
 
• The Vedic texts were transmitted orally for centuries before being written down.
 
• The recitation techniques helped preserve their integrity despite the absence of written scripts.
 
 
 
• **Key Recitation Styles:**
 
 
• **Samhita Patha:** Continuous recitation of the text as written.
 
• **Krama Patha:** Reciting words in a sequential overlapping manner, e.g., AB, BC, CD.
 
• **Ghana Patha:** A complex style that repeats words in specific patterns for accuracy.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• In 2008, the tradition of Vedic chanting was inscribed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
 
• This recognition highlights its significance as one of the oldest unbroken oral traditions in the world.

questions.question: Who administered the agrahara lands during the post-Gupta period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the post-Gupta period, **agrahara lands were granted to Brahmins** as a mark of respect and for religious purposes.
 
• Brahmins, as recipients of these lands, **held administrative and fiscal control** over the agrahara lands.
 
• These lands were exempted from taxation, and Brahmins were responsible for **managing agricultural production and collecting revenue**.
 
• The grants were often documented on copper plates and were intended to **support Brahmins in their religious and scholarly duties**.
 
• The agrahara system played a crucial role in **strengthening Brahminical influence** and promoting Vedic traditions in society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agrahara Lands**:

 
 
• Agrahara refers to villages or lands granted to Brahmins by rulers for religious and educational purposes.
 
• These lands were typically tax-free and were intended to support Brahmins economically.
 
 
 
• **Post-Gupta Period**:
 
 
• This period (circa 6th to 12th century CE) saw the rise of feudal practices and decentralization of authority.
 
• Land grants, including agrahara lands, became a common feature of administration.
 
 
 
• **Brahmins’ Role**:
 
 
• Brahmins were not only religious leaders but also managed the administration of granted lands.
 
• They contributed to the spread of Sanskrit education and upheld Vedic traditions.
 
 
 
• **Feudal Lords and Village Assemblies**:
 
 
• While feudal lords and village assemblies played roles in governance, they were not directly involved in the administration of agrahara lands.
 
• These entities managed other aspects of rural administration.

questions.question: Whom did Chandragupta II marry after defeating the Saka king?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kubernaga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chandragupta II, also known as Vikramaditya, married Princess Kubernaga after defeating the Saka king.
 
• Kubernaga was a Naga princess from the Naga dynasty, which was influential in central India during that era.
 
• This marriage strengthened Chandragupta II's political alliances and helped consolidate his power in the region.
 
• The defeat of the Saka rulers marked a significant milestone in the Gupta Empire's expansion and established its dominance in western India.
 
• Chandragupta II's reign is considered a golden age in Indian history due to advancements in art, culture, and science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saka Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Sakas, also known as Scythians, were an ancient nomadic group who ruled parts of India before being defeated by the Gupta Empire.
 
• The defeat of the Saka rulers by Chandragupta II marked the end of their influence in the region.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire, which spanned from approximately 320 to 550 CE, is often referred to as the "Golden Age of India."
 
• It is known for significant achievements in mathematics, astronomy, literature, and architecture.
 
 
 
• **Naga Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Naga dynasty played a crucial role in regional politics during the Gupta period.
 
• Alliances through marriage, such as Chandragupta II's union with Kubernaga, strengthened ties between the Guptas and Nagas.
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta II:**
 
 
• He was one of the most powerful rulers of the Gupta dynasty and is credited with expanding the empire significantly.
 
• His court was adorned with scholars like Kalidasa and Aryabhata, who contributed to India's cultural and scientific heritage.

questions.question: The Abhidhamma Pitaka explores which of the following areas in depth?

options.text: Ethics, mental phenomena, and psychological insights

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethics, mental phenomena, and psychological insights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Abhidhamma Pitaka is one of the three sections of the Tripitaka, the foundational texts of Theravāda Buddhism.
 
• It focuses on **philosophical and psychological analysis** of the mind, mental phenomena, and ethical principles.
 
• It provides a detailed categorization of mental states, cognitive processes, and ethical behavior.
 
• Unlike the Sutta Pitaka, which contains discourses, the Abhidhamma Pitaka offers a more systematic and analytical approach to Buddhist teachings.
 
• It is considered a scholarly and advanced text, aimed primarily at monks and serious students of Buddhist philosophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tripitaka (Three Baskets):**

 
 
• The Tripitaka consists of three main collections: Vinaya Pitaka (rules for monastic discipline), Sutta Pitaka (Buddha's discourses), and Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical and psychological analysis).
 
• It forms the doctrinal foundation of Theravāda Buddhism and is written in Pali.
 
 
 
• **Abhidhamma Pitaka Structure:**
 
 
• Contains seven books, such as Dhammasangani, Vibhanga, and Patthana, which systematically explore mental and physical phenomena.
 
• Focuses on understanding reality through an analysis of consciousness, perception, and causality.
 
 
 
• **Role in Buddhist Practice:**
 
 
• The Abhidhamma Pitaka helps practitioners cultivate insight (vipassana) into the nature of reality and achieve liberation (nirvana).
 
• It is used as a guide for meditation and ethical living, emphasizing mindfulness and understanding of mental states.
 
 
 
• **Psychological Insights:**
 
 
• Offers a detailed examination of the mind, emotions, and thought processes, making it highly relevant in modern psychological studies.
 
• Its teachings on impermanence (anicca), suffering (dukkha), and non-self (anatta) are central to Buddhist philosophy.

questions.question: An internal trade route during the post-Mauryan empires, Uttarapatha, connected the:

options.text: western and southern parts of India
southern and eastern parts of India
northern and southern parts of India with the northwestern region
northern and eastern parts of India with the northwestern region

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**northern and eastern parts of India with the northwestern region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uttarapatha** was one of the most important trade routes in ancient India, especially during the post-Mauryan period.
 
• It connected the **northern and eastern regions of India with the northwestern region**, facilitating trade and cultural exchanges.
 
• This route extended from the Gangetic plains to the northwestern regions, including **Taxila and regions in present-day Pakistan**.
 
• Uttarapatha was a crucial trade corridor for goods like textiles, spices, and precious metals.
 
• It also played a role in the spread of Buddhism and other cultural influences along its path during the post-Mauryan period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Major Ancient Trade Routes:**

 
 
• **Dakshinapatha:** Connected the southern regions of India to the northern parts.
 
• **Silk Route:** Facilitated trade between India, Central Asia, and China, primarily for silk, spices, and precious stones.
 
• **Grand Trunk Road:** An important ancient route later developed into a major highway during the Mughal period.
 
 
 
• **Taxila's Role:**
 
 
• Taxila, located near Uttarapatha, was a major center for trade and learning during ancient times.
 
• It served as a hub for merchants traveling along Uttarapatha.
 
 
 
• **Post-Mauryan Period:**
 
 
• The post-Mauryan period saw significant trade activity along Uttarapatha under rulers like the Shungas, Kushans, and Satavahanas.
 
• It was during this period that Indian merchants actively engaged in international trade.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism's Spread:**
 
 
• Uttarapatha played a role in the spread of Buddhism to Central Asia and beyond.
 
• Buddhist monks often traveled along this route to propagate teachings.

questions.question: Mihira Bhoja, a famous ruler of the Pratiharas, adopted which title?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adivaraha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mihira Bhoja, one of the most notable rulers of the Pratihara dynasty, adopted the title **Adivaraha**, which symbolized his association with Lord Vishnu's Varaha (boar) incarnation.
 
• The title "Adivaraha" reflects the ruler's dedication to Vaishnavism, which was a significant aspect of his reign.
 
• Mihira Bhoja was known for strengthening the Pratihara dynasty's power and expanding its territorial reach during the 9th century CE.
 
• His reign is marked by significant advancements in administration, military organization, and cultural development under the Pratiharas.
 
• The use of the title "Adivaraha" was also an assertion of divine legitimacy and authority over his kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pratihara Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty was one of the three main powers of early medieval India, alongside the Palas and Rashtrakutas.
 
• Their empire extended over northern and western India, and they were known for their resistance to Arab invasions.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism:**
 
 
• A major tradition within Hinduism that worships Vishnu and his avatars, such as Rama and Krishna, as the supreme deities.
 
• It played a significant role in shaping the religious and cultural practices of medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Varaha Avatar:**
 
 
• Varaha is the third avatar of Vishnu, depicted as a boar that rescued the Earth (personified as the goddess Bhudevi) from the demon Hiranyaksha.
 
• This avatar signifies the triumph of good over evil and the restoration of cosmic order (dharma).
 
 
 
• **Mihira Bhoja's Legacy:**
 
 
• He is celebrated for his military conquests and efficient administration.
 
• His empire acted as a crucial cultural and political bridge between different regions of India during his rule.

questions.question: The 'Tirabhukti' mentioned in Gupta inscriptions corresponds to present-day ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Tirabhukti'** is an ancient term mentioned in Gupta inscriptions referring to a region in present-day Bihar.
 
• The term is derived from Sanskrit, where **'Tira' means bank and 'Bhukti' means enjoyment or territory**, signifying a region associated with riverbanks.
 
• This region was strategically important during the Gupta Empire due to its fertile plains and proximity to the Ganges River.
 
• Historical records suggest that 'Tirabhukti' was part of the administrative structure of the Gupta dynasty, which divided its empire into several provinces or 'Bhuktis.'
 
• Prominent cities in the region during the Gupta period include Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) and Vaishali.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Empire:**

 
 
• The Gupta Empire (circa 320-550 CE) is considered a golden age of Indian culture, art, science, and literature.
 
• It was marked by significant advancements in mathematics, astronomy, and medicine.
 
• The administrative divisions of the empire included provinces called 'Bhuktis,' which were further subdivided into districts called 'Vishayas.'
 
 
 
• **Pataliputra:**
 
 
• Located in modern-day Patna, Pataliputra was a major political and cultural center during the Gupta period.
 
• It served as the capital of several ancient Indian dynasties, including the Mauryas and the Guptas.
 
 
 
• **Vaishali:**
 
 
• An ancient city in Bihar, Vaishali was significant during the Gupta period and earlier.
 
• It is known for its connection to Buddhism and Jainism, with Lord Mahavira spending much of his life there.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Inscriptions:**
 
 
• These inscriptions provide critical insights into the administrative, social, and economic structure of the Gupta Empire.
 
• They are primarily written in Sanskrit and often carved on stone and metal surfaces.

questions.question: The Chalukyas of Badami were founded by:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Pulakesin I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pulakesin I** was the founder of the **Chalukya dynasty**, which ruled primarily in the region of **Badami** in Karnataka.
 
• He established the Chalukya rule around the early **6th century CE**.
 
• Pulakesin I was renowned for his administrative skills and laid the foundation for a strong and centralized kingdom in the Deccan region.
 
• The Chalukyas of Badami are known for their contributions to **art, architecture, and culture**, particularly during their rule in South India.
 
• The Chalukya dynasty under Pulakesin I initiated the tradition of constructing rock-cut temples and monuments, which became iconic in Indian architecture.
 
• Badami, also known as **Vatapi**, served as the capital of the Chalukyas and became a center of political and cultural activities.
 
• Pulakesin I set the stage for the later achievements of his successors, including **Pulakesin II**, who expanded the empire significantly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kirttivarman I**__

 __
 
• **Kirttivarman I** was a successor in the Chalukya dynasty and ruled after Pulakesin I.
 
• He expanded the Chalukya empire and consolidated its power in the Deccan region.

questions.question: The 'Reclining Statue of Lord Vishnu' is found in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Undavalli caves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Reclining Statue of Lord Vishnu" is located in the **Undavalli caves**, situated in the Guntur district of Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• This statue is a prominent example of ancient Indian rock-cut architecture, carved out of a single block of granite.
 
• The statue depicts Lord Vishnu in a reclining posture, also known as **Anantasayana**, resting on the serpent Adishesha.
 
• The Undavalli caves date back to the **4th-5th century CE** and were originally associated with Buddhist monks before being adapted for Hindu worship.
 
• The caves are classified as **monolithic rock-cut architecture** and are considered a significant heritage site in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Undavalli Caves:**

 
 
• The caves are a fine example of **Gupta period architecture**, which reflects the transition from Buddhism to Hinduism in ancient India.
 
• They are multi-storied caves, with the largest one containing the iconic statue of Lord Vishnu in a reclining posture.
 
• The caves were initially built as Buddhist monasteries and later converted into Hindu temples.
 
• The site is under the protection of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**.
 
 
 
• **Reclining Vishnu (Anantasayana):**
 
 
• The posture symbolizes Lord Vishnu resting on the serpent Adishesha, representing cosmic balance and preservation.
 
• It is a recurring theme in Hindu temple sculptures, signifying the sustainer of the universe.
 
 
 
• **Rock-Cut Architecture:**
 
 
• This architectural style involves carving temples, monasteries, or sculptures directly out of natural rock formations.
 
• Famous examples in India include the Ajanta caves, Ellora caves, and Elephanta caves.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Caves in India:**
 
 
• **Ajanta Caves:** Known for Buddhist frescoes and paintings.
 
• **Ellora Caves:** Famous for Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist rock-cut temples, including the Kailasa temple.
 
• **Elephanta Caves:** Located near Mumbai, showcasing Hindu Shaivite sculptures.

questions.question: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is associated with which region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is linked to the ancient region of **Gandhara**, which was located in the present-day areas of northern Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan.
 
• Takht-i-Bahi is a **Buddhist monastic complex** known for its historical and archaeological significance, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
 
• The inscription and site date back to the **Kushan period**, reflecting the flourishing of Buddhism in Gandhara during this era.
 
• Gandhara was a key center for the dissemination of Buddhist art, culture, and teachings, heavily influenced by Greek and Hellenistic styles due to Alexander the Great's incursions into the region.
 
• Takht-i-Bahi remains one of the most well-preserved monastic complexes from the Gandhara period, providing valuable insights into ancient Buddhist practices and architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhara Art**

 
 
• Gandhara art is known for its fusion of **Indian and Hellenistic influences**, creating unique representations of Buddhist iconography.
 
• It played a significant role in the development of Buddhist sculpture, particularly the depiction of the Buddha in human form.
 
• The art is characterized by intricate carvings, reliefs, and statues made from stone, stucco, and clay.
 
 
 
• **Kushan Empire**
 
 
• The Kushan Empire ruled over Gandhara during the 1st-3rd centuries CE, promoting Buddhism and trade along the Silk Road.
 
• Kushan rulers, such as Kanishka, were instrumental in spreading Buddhism to Central Asia and China.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status**
 
 
• Takht-i-Bahi was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1980** due to its historical, cultural, and architectural importance.
 
• The site includes stupas, monastic cells, meditation halls, and assembly areas, showcasing the monastic lifestyle of ancient Buddhist practitioners.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Monastic Practices**
 
 
• Buddhist monasteries like Takht-i-Bahi served as centers for religious education, meditation, and community welfare.
 
• Monks followed strict routines of study and meditation while adhering to the teachings of the Buddha.
 
• Such sites were funded by local rulers, merchants, and pilgrims who supported the spread of Buddhism.

questions.question: Who discovered the Maski Ashoka Inscription?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C Beadon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maski inscription was discovered by **C Beadon** in the year **1915**.
 
• It is located in **Maski**, a village in the Raichur district of Karnataka, India.
 
• The inscription is significant as it is the first Ashokan edict where the emperor is referred to by his personal name, **Ashoka**, instead of his titles.
 
• The Maski inscription belongs to the **Minor Rock Edict series**, which provides insight into Ashoka's policies promoting Dhamma (moral conduct).
 
• This discovery helped confirm that the King referred to in various edicts across India was indeed **Emperor Ashoka**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **James Prinsep**

 
 
• James Prinsep was an English scholar and orientalist who deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1837.
 
• His work laid the foundation for understanding Ashokan inscriptions and the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Edicts**
 
 
• The Ashokan edicts are inscriptions carved on rocks, pillars, and caves across India during Emperor Ashoka's reign (268–232 BCE).
 
• They propagate the principles of Dhamma, including non-violence, respect for all life forms, and social harmony.
 
 
 
• **Minor Rock Edicts**
 
 
• These are brief inscriptions primarily addressing the importance of moral conduct and Dhamma.
 
• They differ from Major Rock Edicts, which cover administrative policies and broader principles.
 
 
 
• **Christian Lassen**
 
 
• Christian Lassen was a German Indologist known for his work on Sanskrit and ancient Indian history.
 
• He contributed to the study of Indian inscriptions but did not discover the Maski inscription.

questions.question: In the Harappan civilisation, cire perdue or lost wax process was used to make statue of which material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bronze**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The lost wax technique, also known as **cire perdue**, was used during the Harappan civilization for crafting **bronze statues**.
 
• One of the most famous examples is the **"Dancing Girl"**, a bronze figurine discovered at Mohenjo-Daro, showcasing the advanced metalworking skills of the Harappans.
 
• This technique involved creating a wax model, covering it with clay or another mold material, and then heating it so the wax melts and is replaced by molten metal.
 
• The process allowed for intricate designs and demonstrated the Harappans' mastery in metallurgy and art.
 
• The use of bronze highlights the significance of alloy-making and metal technology in the Harappan civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bronze:**

 
 
• Bronze is an alloy primarily consisting of copper and tin, known for its durability and corrosion resistance.
 
• It was widely used in ancient civilizations, including the Harappans, for making tools, weapons, and artistic objects.
 
• Bronze enabled the creation of detailed sculptures and was integral to trade and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Lost Wax Technique (Cire Perdue):**
 
 
• The technique dates back thousands of years and is still used in modern sculpture-making.
 
• The process involves multiple steps, including creating a wax model, molding, and casting with metal.
 
• It allows for precision and intricate design, making it ideal for artistic expression.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Art and Craft:**
 
 
• The Harappan civilization was renowned for its craftsmanship in pottery, bead-making, metallurgy, and sculpture.
 
• The artifacts reflect their advanced skills, artistic sensibilities, and technological innovations.
 
• Materials like terracotta, stone, and metals were used extensively in their art and daily life.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Mohenjo-Daro:**
 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro is one of the largest settlements of the Indus Valley Civilization and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• It has yielded numerous artifacts, including the famous "Dancing Girl" statue, which offers insight into Harappan culture.
 
• The site demonstrates the urban planning and artistic achievements of the civilization.

__
 
• The title **Prathamakayastha** was used to denote the head of the Kayastha community during ancient and medieval periods in India.
 
• The Kayastha community was traditionally associated with administrative and clerical roles in the bureaucracy of Indian kingdoms.
 
• The Prathamakayastha oversaw the functioning of scribes, record keepers, and other clerical staff within the administrative framework.
 
• Kayasthas were regarded as a literate and influential community due to their expertise in management, accounting, and record-keeping.
 
• This community played a significant role in maintaining governance and administration, especially during the Gupta period and later in medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kayastha Community:**

 
 
• The Kayasthas are a prominent community in India traditionally linked to the roles of scribes and administrators.
 
• They gained prominence during the Gupta period and later became key figures in the Mughal and British administrations.
 
• Kayasthas were known for their proficiency in multiple languages, including Sanskrit, Persian, and local dialects.
 
 
 
• **Prathamakayastha Role:**
 
 
• The Prathamakayastha acted as the chief of the Kayastha scribes and administrators, ensuring accuracy in record-keeping and governance.
 
• This role required expertise in legal, financial, and administrative matters.
 
 
 
• **Other Titles:**
 
 
• Titles like **Prathamakulika** and **Pustapala** were also used for administrative officers, but they differed in function from Prathamakayastha.
 
• Prathamakulika often referred to senior officers, while Pustapala was responsible for maintaining records and archives.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The administrative expertise of Kayasthas contributed significantly to the efficiency of Indian kingdoms.
 
• Their influence extended beyond administration into fields like literature, law, and governance.

questions.question: Who succeeded Ashoka to the throne?

__
 
• **Dasharatha succeeded Emperor Ashoka** to the throne of the Maurya Empire in approximately **232 BCE**.
 
• He was the grandson of Ashoka and ruled the eastern part of the Mauryan Empire, including Magadha.
 
• Dasharatha is known for continuing Ashoka’s policy of spreading Buddhism and maintaining the empire's stability during his reign.
 
• Inscriptions such as the** Nagarjuni Hills cave inscriptions **suggest Dasharatha dedicated these caves to the **Ajivikas**, a sect patronized by Ashoka as well.
 
• Dasharatha’s reign marked the beginning of the decline of the Mauryan Empire, as it became fragmented after Ashoka's death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka’s Contributions:**

 
 
• Ashoka was one of the greatest emperors in Indian history, known for his role in spreading Buddhism across Asia.
 
• His reign marked the peak of the Mauryan Empire's territorial expansion and administrative efficiency.
 
• The Edicts of Ashoka, inscribed on rocks and pillars, reflect his policies of Dhamma and social welfare.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire Decline:**
 
 
• After Ashoka's death, the Mauryan Empire gradually weakened due to internal divisions and lack of strong leadership.
 
• The empire fragmented into smaller kingdoms, leading to the rise of regional powers such as the Shunga Dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Ajivikas Sect:**
 
 
• The Ajivikas were an ascetic sect contemporary to Buddhism and Jainism during Ashoka's time.
 
• They believed in the doctrine of niyati (predestination), which emphasized fate as the ultimate factor in life.
 
 
 
• **Nagarjuni Hills Inscriptions:**
 
 
• These inscriptions are attributed to Dasharatha and are located in Bihar, India.
 
• The caves were dedicated to Ajivikas and reflect Mauryan architectural and religious influence.

questions.question: Which Harappan site shows evidence of ploughed fields?

__
 
• **Kalibangan** is a prominent Harappan site located in present-day Rajasthan, India.
 
• It is unique among Harappan sites for providing evidence of **ploughed agricultural fields**.
 
• The ploughed field marks at Kalibangan are indicative of early agricultural practices in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• These field impressions were discovered near the southern part of the site, showing **furrows aligned in two directions**, suggesting advanced farming techniques.
 
• The discovery highlights the significance of agriculture in the economy of the Harappan civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**:

 
 
• It is one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, dating back to** 2500 BCE**.
 
• Major sites include **Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, Lothal, and Kalibangan**.
 
• Known for advanced town planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures.
 
 
 
• **Kalibangan’s Historical Significance**:
 
 
• Kalibangan is divided into two parts: the **citadel **(western mound) and the **lower town** (eastern mound).
 
• The site shows evidence of fire altars, indicating ritualistic practices.
 
• It also provides evidence of mud-brick structures typical of Harappan architecture.
 
 
 
• **Ploughed Fields in Archaeology**:
 
 
• Ploughed field impressions are rare in archaeology and provide insights into ancient agricultural practices.
 
• Such discoveries help reconstruct the methods of crop cultivation used by early civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture in the Harappan Civilization**:
 
 
• Major crops included **wheat, barley, sesame, mustard, and cotton**.
 
• Advanced irrigation techniques and seasonal cultivation were practiced.
 
• Kalibangan’s evidence of ploughed fields complements the broader understanding of Harappan agriculture.

questions.question: The Maski Ashoka Inscription is situated in which state of India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maski Ashoka Inscription is located in **Maski village** of Raichur district in the state of **Karnataka, India**.
 
• This inscription is significant as it was the first to explicitly mention the name **Ashoka**, identifying him with the title "Devanampiya Piyadasi" (Beloved of the Gods).
 
• The Maski inscription was discovered by **C. Beadon** in 1915, and it played a crucial role in confirming the identity of Ashoka as the ruler responsible for the edicts.
 
• It is one of the **Minor Rock Edicts** of Ashoka and promotes the principles of Dhamma (righteousness).
 
• The inscription is written in the **Prakrit language** using the Brahmi script, which was widely used during the Mauryan period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka and His Edicts:**

 
 
• Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, ruled during the 3rd century BCE and is renowned for his promotion of Buddhism and Dhamma (moral conduct).
 
• His inscriptions, known as **Ashokan Edicts**, are spread across the Indian subcontinent and are categorized into Major Rock Edicts, Minor Rock Edicts, Pillar Edicts, and Cave Inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Maski Inscription:**
 
 
• Before the Maski discovery, it was unclear whether "Devanampiya Piyadasi" referred to Ashoka or another ruler.
 
• The Maski edict confirmed that "Devanampiya Piyadasi" was indeed **Ashoka**, solidifying his connection with the inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Prakrit and Brahmi:**
 
 
• **Prakrit** was the common language of the people during the Mauryan period, used in many of Ashoka's edicts.
 
• **Brahmi script** is one of the oldest writing systems in India, serving as the precursor to many modern Indian scripts.
 
 
 
• **Raichur District:**
 
 
• Raichur is located in northern Karnataka and is historically significant due to its association with several ancient kingdoms, including the Mauryas.
 
• It is home to many archaeological and historical sites, including the Maski inscription.

• The Maitrakas ruled from their capital at **Valabhi**, located in present-day Gujarat, which became an important center of trade and learning.
 
• Valabhi was known for its **Buddhist monasteries and learning institutions**, drawing scholars and monks from across India.
 
• The Maitrakas played a key role in maintaining regional stability and fostering cultural and economic growth in western India.

• **Gupta Empire:**

 
 
• The Gupta Empire (320-550 CE) is often referred to as the **Golden Age of India** due to advancements in science, art, mathematics, and literature.
 
• Feudatories like the Maitrakas initially served under the Guptas, managing smaller regions within the empire.
 
• The decline of Gupta power led to the emergence of several independent regional kingdoms, including the Maitrakas.
 
 
 
• **Valabhi:**
 
 
• Valabhi was a prominent city and the capital of the Maitrakas, located in modern-day Gujarat.
 
• The city was renowned for its **Buddhist universities**, comparable to Nalanda in eastern India.
 
• Valabhi played a significant role in regional trade and cultural exchanges during the Maitraka rule.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism and Trade:**
 
 
• The Maitrakas were patrons of Buddhism and supported the construction of monasteries and educational institutions.
 
• Valabhi became a hub for Buddhist scholars and monks, contributing to the spread of Buddhist teachings.
 
• The kingdom's location along trade routes fostered economic prosperity and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Decline:**
 
 
• The Maitrakas ruled until the **8th century CE**, after which they were overpowered by the Arabs and other emerging forces.
 
• Their contributions to culture and education left a lasting legacy in western India.
